questions.stem: How does Transport Canada define fatigue, and since when has fatigue management in the marine sector been on the TSB Watchlist?
options: Less mental or physical ability from sleep factors; 2018
Muscle soreness after heavy work on deck; since 2005
A medical condition that needs treatment; since 2010
Reduced eyesight at night on watch; since 2015
questions.explanation: Fatigue is reduced mental or physical ability from sleep-related factors, and the issue has been on the TSB Watchlist since 2018. The other definitions and dates are invented.

questions.stem: Which of these counts as hours of rest under the regulation?
options: Any time not at the wheel, including coffee breaks on watch
Time spent in the mess during a watch
The first 5 minutes of every hour worked
Time outside hours of work, not short breaks
questions.explanation: Hours of rest means rest time outside hours of work and does not include short breaks.

questions.stem: A crew member on a near coastal voyage in Canadian waters has a schedule that gives only 4 hours of rest as the longest uninterrupted block each day, with 10 hours of rest in total. What does the domestic hours of rest rule require?
options: Any 8 hours in 24, in any blocks, so this passes
At least 12 consecutive hours of rest, so this fails
At least 6 consecutive hours in 24, so this fails
At least 10 hours in total in 24, so this passes
questions.explanation: Section 320 requires at least 6 consecutive hours of rest in every 24 hours and 16 hours of rest in every 48. A longest block of 4 hours does not meet the consecutive-hours test even if the total is higher.

questions.stem: On domestic voyages, how long may elapse between the end of one rest period and the start of the next?
options: Not less than 12 hours, and not more than 24
Not more than 18 hours, and not less than 6 hours
Not more than 14 hours, and not less than 8
Not more than 24 hours, whatever the voyage
questions.explanation: Section 320 says not more than 18 but not less than 6 hours between rest periods. The 14-hour figure is the s. 321 interval for unlimited voyages.

questions.stem: Which statement matches the rule for unlimited voyages (s. 321)?
options: Max 14 h work in 24 and 72 in 7 days, or min 10 h rest in 24 and 77 in 7
At least 6 consecutive hours of rest in 24 and at least 16 hours in 48
No more than 12 hours of work in any 24 and no more than 60 in 7 days
At least 8 hours of rest in any 24 and at least 56 hours in 7 days
questions.explanation: Section 321 gives two alternatives: 14/72 limits on work, or 10/77 minimums of rest. The 6 and 16 figures are the domestic rule.

questions.stem: On an unlimited voyage a crew member works 0600-1800 and 2000-0200 each day. Which statement is correct?
options: The schedule passes because it is split into two work blocks
The schedule passes because the rest period is at least 6 hours
The schedule passes as long as the crew member is only on call
It fails: 18 h of work is over 14, and 6 h rest is under 10
questions.explanation: Work is 12 + 6 = 18 hours, which exceeds 14, and rest is 24 − 18 = 6 hours, below 10. So both the work limit and the rest minimum are failed.

questions.stem: On unlimited voyages, how must the rest hours be divided?
options: One single block of 10 hours, taken at night
Three periods of 3 hours each, spread over the day
Two periods at most, one of 6 h+, gaps of 14 h max
Into any number of periods of at least one hour each
questions.explanation: Section 321(2) says no more than two rest periods, one at least 6 hours, and no more than 14 hours between consecutive rest periods.

questions.stem: When scheduling work and rest, whose fatigue must the master consider especially?
options: Only crew who are on their very first trip
Crew with navigational or safe operation duties
Only the master's own fatigue, as the one in command
Only engine room crew working in the heat
questions.explanation: Section 322 says the danger of fatigue, especially for those whose duties involve navigational safety and safe operation, must be taken into account.

questions.stem: A vessel in trouble needs all hands to help a boat in distress for 9 hours. Which statement about the rest schedule is correct?
options: Suspend it, then give compensatory rest when feasible
The rest rules cannot be suspended in any circumstances at all
The master may suspend the schedule and no compensatory rest is needed
Rules bind only the master
questions.explanation: The master may suspend the schedule for the immediate safety of the vessel or persons, or to help others in distress, but compensatory rest must follow as soon as feasible.

questions.stem: Which of these is true about fatigue training and records?
options: No records are needed if the voyage is under 24 hours, and the e-course is optional
Records are kept only for officers, and the e-course must be repeated every year
The e-course must be paid for by the seafarer and expires after 5 years
Master keeps daily hours records; MED students take the e-course
questions.explanation: Section 323 requires the record until discharge. Transport Canada requires the free CCOHS e-course before the MED certificate is issued, and says the course certificate does not expire.
